title: Tune-A-Video: One-Shot Tuning of Image Diffusion Models for Text-to-Video Generation
grouping: A narrow left column and a wide right grid. The left column stacks an orange rounded 'Tune-A-Video' box with a flame icon, a plus sign, and a dashed rounded grey container holding three blue bow-tie shapes labelled 'Pretrained T2I' (plain, personalised for a style, with pose control), each with small example images. The right grid has five rows of six frames: the source clip on top with small down-arrows under each frame, then four generated clips, each introduced by a centred prompt line between the rows.
shapes_depth: Photographic frames of equal size with thin white gutters; no boxes around rows. Prompts are written in a handwritten italic face in quotes, with the words that changed from the source prompt coloured blue. One row adds a strip of black pose-skeleton thumbnails after its prompt, joined by a plus sign. The model components on the left are flat filled shapes with white bold text.
proposed_highlight: The method itself is the single orange box at the top of the left column, set apart from the blue pretrained models in the dashed container below it by a plus sign. In the grid, the edits are carried by blue words in each prompt line.
lesson: In a video-editing teaser, put the source clip as the top row of frames with small down-arrows to the edited rows below, and introduce each edited row with its prompt written between the rows with only the changed words coloured.
notes: Venue ICCV from Semantic Scholar title match; year = arXiv preprint year (2212.11565). Mostly photographic content.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
